```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
bp <- read_csv(here::here("data/bonita_peak.csv"))
categories <- read_csv(here::here("data/site_categories.csv"))
```

```{r}

bp |>
  left_join(categories) |>
  distinct(site_id, taxon, site_cat2) |>
  group_by(site_id, site_cat2) |>
  summarise(total_rich = n()) |>
ggplot(
       aes(x = site_id,
           y = total_rich,
           fill = site_cat2)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Total Richness",
y = "Richness")
```

## Overview

You will calculate some simple metrics for (nearly) the complete Bonita Peak data set. The calculations will largely follow the first tutorial from class. The second tutorial will show some examples for calculating these metrics across the full data set. In addition to your calculations, you will develop a multi-metric index and apply it to some "test" sites with unknown environmental condition. Finally, you will interpret the condition in these unknown sites in your write up.

## Set up

-   Load the `tidyverse` library

-   Read in the data

```{r}
#| eval: false
# library
library(tidyverse)

# data
bp <- read_csv("data/bonita_peak.csv")
categories <- read_csv("data/site_categories.csv")
```

## Modify data to add categories and remove `test` sites

-   Join the `bp` and the `categories` data together

```{r}
full_dat <- bp |>
  full_join(categories)
full_dat
```

-   Make two objects

    -   One which does not have data from the `test` sites

    -   One that only has the `test` sites

```{r}
fit_dat <-  full_dat |>
  filter(site_category != "test")
fit_dat
test_dat <- full_dat |>
  filter(site_category == "test")
test_dat
```

# Calculations

-   Complete the following calculations.

-   You should save your results for each problem in a new data object.

    -   i.e., store the results of problem 1 in an object called `total_rich`, the results for problem 2 as `EPT_rich`, etc.

-   Based on your results, you will pick 5 metrics which most closely align with the site category designations

-   You will determine index values based on the numbers in your results.

    -   score of 1 = mean `reference` value

    -   score of 3 = mean `light` value

    -   Score of 5 = mean `heavy` value

-   Then, you will calculate an average index value for each category

-   Finally, you will calculate an average index value for your `test` sites and interpret their overall condition.

-   When the question asks for you to make a plot, ensure the following

    -   The plot has an appropriate title

    -   The plot has a descriptive name on the y-axis

    -   Your saved plots are a reasonable size

        -   After you export the plot, look at it and paste it into your submission document

        -   You may need to re-save the plot with different `height` and `width` values.

## Richness

1.  Calculate the total richness in your two sites. Make sure to save it as a data object. In addition, make a bar graph of this result and save it as a .png file to your `plots/` folder.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
total_rich <- fit_dat |>
  distinct(site_id, taxon, site_cat2) |>
  group_by(site_id, site_cat2) |>
  summarise(total_rich = n())
# total_rich
# ggplot(total_rich,
#        aes(x = site_id, 
#            y = total_rich,
#            fill = site_category)) +
#   geom_col() +
#   labs(title = "Total Richness",
       # y = "Richness")


ggplot(total_rich,
       aes(y = total_rich,
           fill = site_cat2)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Total Richness",
       y = "Richness")

total_rich |>
  group_by(site_cat2) |>
  summarize(mean(total_rich),sd(total_rich))

# ref = 26.2 
# light = 20.7 
# heavy = 10
```

2.  Calculate the EPT richness in your two sites and save it as a data object.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ept_rich <- fit_dat |>
  filter(order == "Ephemeroptera" |
           order == "Plecoptera" |
           order == "Trichoptera") |>
  distinct(site_category, stream, taxon) |>
  group_by(site_category, stream) |>
  summarise(EPT_rich = n()) |>
  ungroup()

ept_rich |>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(EPT_rich))
# 15.8, 12.4, 5.17
  
```

4.  Calculate the richness of the Rhyacophilidae family in your two sites. In addition, make a bar graph of this result and save it as a .png file to your `plots/` folder.

```{r}
#| message: false

  filter(family == "Rhyacophilidae") |>
  distinct(site_category, stream, taxon) |>
  group_by(site_category, stream) |>
  summarise(rhya_rich = n())

rhya_rich |>
```

5.  Calculate the per cent of EPT individuals for your two sites and save it as a data object. In addition, make a bar graph of this result and save it as a .png file to your `plots/` folder.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ept_per_n <- fit_dat |>
  filter(order == "Ephemeroptera" |
           order == "Plecoptera" |
           order == "Trichoptera") |>
  group_by(site_category, stream, total_count) |>
  summarize(ept_n = sum(count)) |>
  mutate(ept_percent_ind = ept_n / total_count)

ept_per_n |>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(ept_percent_ind))

# 0.811, 0.837, 0.539
```

6.  Calculate the per cent of individuals which are in the Chironomidae family in your two sites and save it as an object.

```{r}
chiro_per_n <- fit_dat |>
  filter(family == "Chironomidae") |>
  group_by(stream, site_category, total_count) |>
  summarize(chiro_n = sum(count)) |>
  mutate(chiro_percent_ind = chiro_n / total_count)

chiro_per_n |>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(chiro_percent_ind))

```

6.  Calculate Shannon's Diversity Index and save it as a data object. In addition, make a bar graph of this result and save it as a .png file to your `plots/` folder.

```{r}
shannon <- fit_dat |> 
  select(stream, site_category, taxon, count, total_count) |>
  mutate(pi = count / total_count,
         ln_pi = log(pi),
         pi_ln_pi = pi*ln_pi) |>
  group_by(stream, site_category) |>
  summarize(H = -sum(pi_ln_pi))
shannon

ggplot(shannon,
       aes(x = stream, 
           y = H)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Shannon's Diversity Index",
       y = "H`")

ggplot(shannon,
       aes(x = site_category, 
           y = H)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Shannon's Diversity Index",
       y = "H`")

shannon |>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(H))

# 2.26, 2.22, 1.81
```

7.  Calculate the richness of the predator functional feeding group in your two sites and save it as an object.

```{r}
pred_rich <- fit_dat |>
    filter(FFG == "predator") |>
    distinct(stream, taxon, site_category) |>
    group_by(stream, site_category) |>
    summarise(pred_rich = n())
pred_rich|>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(pred_rich))

# 7.67, 5.6, 3.33

fit_dat |>
    filter(FFG == "scraper") |>
    distinct(stream, taxon, site_category) |>
    group_by(stream, site_category) |>
    summarise(pred_rich = n()) |>
  group_by(site_category) |>
  summarize(mean(pred_rich))
# 4, 3.2, 1

```
